title: kernel-scout-autotune-strategies-for-mixed-prefill-decode
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: mixed prefill/decode workloads show highly variable kernel performance across hardware and sequence-length distributions. Existing knob-based kernel routing is brittle for bursty user traffic and varied token-phase behavior (long prefill, short decode or vice versa). Goal: implement a lightweight, production-safe autotuner ("Kernel Scout") that continuously scores candidate kernels per model/arch/seqlen bucket and nudges routing policies using a confidence-weighted bandit + microprobe system. Scope: scoring heuristics, warmstart multipliers, fragmentation-aware occupancy estimator, and a low-risk rollout path for canary traffic.
description_short: Implement Kernel Scout: an online autotuner that picks kernels by arch+seqlen+phase using microprobes and a confidence-weighted scoring function.
acceptance_criteria: Kernel Scout runs as an opt-in runtime component and exposes a /probe endpoint for safe microbenches
End-to-end A/B canary over 1% traffic shows no regression in p99 latency (>5% threshold) and reduces median cost-per-1k-tokens for targeted workloads by >=8%
Autotuner persists kernel scores and recovers gracefully after server restarts or model rollouts
Operators can disable exploration or pin kernel choices via Console toggles
Perf dashboard reflects per-kernel p50/p99, probe counts, and confidence metrics
notes: High-level approach: maintain per-(model,arch,seqlen-bucket,phase) candidate list. For each candidate compute a composite score combining latency estimate, cost ratio, fragmentation penalty and a warmstart advantage factor. Use a decaying exploration schedule: initial epsilon=0.25 for new model/version; decay to epsilon=0.02 after N probes or confidence threshold. Store probe history in TTL-backed local store and ship aggregated metrics to Console for visibility.
algorithm_summary: score = w_lat*norm(latency) + w_cost*norm(cost) + w_frag*fragmentation_penalty - w_warm*warm_multiplier; where warm_multiplier>1 decreases score advantage for kernels that only beat others when cache warm. Confidence computed as inverse variance of recent probe latencies; low confidence triggers more probes. Exploration is guided by a softmax over scores with temperature anneal.
experiment_plan: 1) Unit microbench harness for deterministic measurement across arch/seqlen combos. 2) Internal dogfood: run 0.5% traffic for 24h with exploration disabled (only logging) to validate signal. 3) Canary: 1% traffic with exploration enabled and automated rollback if p99 increases >5% at 10-minute check windows. 4) Scale to 5% with staged region rollouts.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: noisy probes may cause flapping kernel switches and increased tail latency. Mitigation: require confidence threshold before applying policy changes, apply hysteresis windows (min 30 minutes between enforced switches), and allow immediate manual pinning via Console. Risk: fragmentation estimator may undercount usable occupancy on GPUs with variable allocator patterns. Mitigation: conservative fragmentation_penalty until validated by microbench sweep and memory-trace correlation.
observability: Instrument probe_count, p50/p90/p99 per-kernel, switch_events, confidence_score, warm_hits, fragmentation_estimate. Add alert rule: if switch_event_rate > 50/hour or p99 regressions exceed 5% vs control, auto-disable exploration and trigger PagerDuty runbook 'KS-AutoTune-Failures'.
ops_playbook: How to disable: Console -> Runtime Features -> Kernel Scout -> toggle off exploration. Rollback: pin previous kernel in routing table. Debug steps: collect /probe logs, attach microbench CSV, run local microbench with same seed and compare. Postmortem template linked in Confluence.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Kickoff: reviewed high-level design with Runtime and Serving teams. Agreed to keep Kernel Scout opt-in initially and to reuse existing metrics export path.
2026-02-25 - Design review: PM asked to include cost-per-1k-tokens as first-class signal; SRE requested hysteresis and explicit disable path. Incorporated both into acceptance criteria.
2026-03-02 - Microbench iteration: found that small-seqlen (<32) kernels show large variance on A100 when occupancy <40%. Added fragmentation estimator and a warmstart multiplier to scoring.
2026-03-05 - Engineering sync: implemented probe endpoint and proto for probe payload. WIP: storage adapter for TTL probe history (Redis candidate).
2026-03-09 - Dogfood run (0.5% logged): initial probes match offline microbench ordering for 78% of buckets; mismatch analysis points to allocator-dependent behavior in 3 GPU instance types.
2026-03-12 - Next: implement confidence-based lock before switch, add Grafana panels for per-bucket switch rate and confidence. Schedule canary for 2026-03-20 if tests pass.
review_feedback: Design: SRE - require Circuit Breaker with auto-disable on repeated regressions (implemented in ops_playbook).
Design: ML infra - ensure model version changes reset warmstart history to avoid stale bias (added to implementation notes).
Design: Cost team - add cost-normalization per-region and per-GPU type when comparing kernels (to prevent cross-hardware bias).
implementation_notes: Persist scores to TTL Redis with keys: ks:<model>:<version>:<arch>:<bucket>
Probe flow: lightweight prefill-only microbench (N=5 samples), decode-only microbench (N=5), combined (N=3); aggregated with trimmed mean
Expose runtime flags: ks.explore=true|false, ks.epsilon=float, ks.min_confidence=int
Add unit tests for score arithmetic and confidence decay
